input.quote: Kubient hereby grants to Customer a limited, royalty-free, non-exclusive, non-transferable, non-assignable, without right of sublicense, revocable license to access, participate in and use to the full extent the Auction Platform as hosted by Kubient,
input.rationale: The Auction Platform grant in paragraph 2 is expressly "revocable" with no limitation to a termination event, which lets Kubient pull the licence at its discretion — walk-away territory under this rule. It also runs to "Customer" only: affiliates and contractors are not named, and paragraph 5(a) affirmatively bars third-party access to the Service absent Kubient's advance written approval, so there is no notice-based path to add affiliates as the fallback requires. Assignment is not the problem — paragraph 12(h) already permits assignment without consent to an affiliate, an asset purchaser or a successor by merger, so the successor-transfer element of the fallback is met. Because the revocability and affiliate/contractor exclusion both fail the fallback, we take the grant to the preferred position: licence extended to AP affiliates and contractors acting on AP's behalf (with a matching carve-out in paragraph 5(a) and AP remaining responsible for their compliance) and revocable only on expiration or termination, which is consistent with paragraph 4(c)(ii) revoking the licence at termination.

proposal.summary: Extend the Auction Platform licence to AP affiliates and contractors acting on AP's behalf and remove Kubient's at-will revocation right
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have extended the licence to our affiliates and to contractors acting on our behalf (with a matching carve-out to the third-party access restriction), and made the licence revocable only on expiration or termination, since our playbook does not accept a licence that Kubient can revoke at will or that excludes the affiliates and vendors who actually operate our properties. If helpful, we can instead cover affiliates on written notice to Kubient.
